title: Incident follow-up: canary rollback simulator, safety lab, and operator training
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Summary: After the staged-model rollout that triggered a noisy, cascading canary rollback on 2025-02-12, we need a structured follow-up that reduces blast radius for future staged deployments. This ticket scopes three deliverables: 1) a Canary Rollback Simulator (CRS) — a replayable harness that runs historical and synthetic traffic through rollout policies and produces deterministic rollback decisions for verification; 2) a Safety Lab runbook and operator playbook with step-by-step diagnostics and post-rollback recovery steps; 3) an operator training session and lightweight exam plus recorded modules for on-call and release engineers.

Goals:
- Make rollback decisions reproducible in a lab to validate new policies before rollout.
- Reduce mean time to safe rollback (MTSR) by 30% in the first quarter after rollout of these tools.
- Reduce false positive automated rollbacks by tightening telemetry and decision hysteresis.

Scope (what we'll build):
- CRS: traffic replayer with configurable cohort sizes, latency/noise injection, and plug-ins for the routing policy engine so it produces the same metric outputs as production. Includes a CLI and CI job that runs on each candidate rollout PR.
- Safety Lab runbook: run-level checklist, top-5 diagnostics (latency distribution, token-level error spikes, KV cache noise), escalation matrix, and standardized rollback verification steps.
- Training: 90-minute live lab + 30-minute recorded walkthrough; practice exercises where engineers run simulated rollouts in CRS and execute manual vs auto rollback scenarios.

Out of scope: full traffic capture plumbing for regulated customers; on-prem private deployment integration will be covered by follow-up ticket if needed.
acceptance_criteria: CRS can replay a 1M request synthetic suite and produce the same routed-model metrics as production within 5% error
CI gate: a candidate model rollout PR runs CRS smoke test and produces pass/fail verdicts visible in the PR
Updated runbook published to Confluence with signoff from SRE and PM
Training delivered to release engineers and a recording stored in the learning portal
Two follow-up on-call rotations run rescue drills using CRS with documented timings
decision_log: 2025-02-20: Decided to prioritise deterministic replay + noise injection rather than full-fidelity capture to keep scope bounded (Priya, Luca, Mei)

2025-02-24: Agreed on rollback decision hysteresis: require sustained metric breach for 2 consecutive evaluation windows (10m windows) before automated rollback (SRE review) — reduces flip-flop risk (SLA trade-off accepted)
2025-02-27: Opted to gate the CRS CI job behind an opt-in flag for initial 2 cycles to tune thresholds without impacting release cadence (PM request)
2025-03-01: Chose cohort-size simulation knobs (0.5%, 2.5%, 10%) for experiment matrix — aligns with prior production cohorts
tradeoffs: Deterministic simulation vs engineering time: investing in CRS increases pre-release time but reduces incident churn
Automated rollback aggressiveness vs availability: longer hysteresis avoids false rollbacks but delays mitigation for real regressions
Synthetic traffic fidelity vs PII concerns: we will use sanitized/synth datasets to avoid storing PII while still exercising model behavior

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: CRS results differ from production due to hidden dependencies (e.g., network topology). Mitigation: instrument small canary runs to produce baselines and iterate on simulator knobs.
Risk: Overfitting rollout policies to simulator behaviour. Mitigation: include historical incident traces (sanitized) and random noise injection in the simulator.
Risk: Teams skip CRS due to added latency in release flow. Mitigation: keep CI smoke as optional for first cycles and provide a fast 'quick-check' mode that runs a 1k-sample subset
notes: We plan to measure success by MTSR and automated rollback precision (false positives / true positives). Baseline will be taken from the 2025-02 incident telemetry.
Follow-ups: integration with Private deployment routing (ENG-xxxx) and a customer-facing KB for Dedicated customers will be scheduled in Q2
